h1: Kao Ngu Boutique Resort — a hillside boutique at Khao Ngu where you wake up to mountain views for a few hundred baht
intro: If you want a Ratchaburi stay that's quiet, close to nature, where you open the door to a real mountain view at a friendly price — Kao Ngu Boutique Resort is a name that visitors to Khao Ngu Stone Park bring up often. It's a small boutique resort of roughly 14-15 rooms set right at the foot of Khao Ngu in Ko Phlapphla. Rooms come with mountain or garden views, air-conditioning, TV and en-suite bathrooms; there's an on-site Thai restaurant, free parking, and one standout that many love — pets are welcome. It's about a 15-minute walk to Khao Ngu Stone Park, and rooms start from approximately THB 590/night, which is a genuine bargain for a hillside stay in Ratchaburi.

body.html: Khao Ngu is a small limestone hill northwest of central Ratchaburi, home to ancient Buddha-image caves, rock-climbing crags, and the Khao Ngu Stone Park that has become one of Ratchaburi's most popular check-in spots in recent years. There aren't many places to stay around here, and Kao Ngu Boutique Resort is one of the few genuinely at the foot of the hill — about a 15-minute walk to the stone park — which makes it a natural pick if you've come specifically for Khao Ngu or just want a one-night stopover along the way.

The resort itself is a small boutique of roughly 14-15 rooms tucked behind the Khao Ngu area. Rooms come in several sizes by price, from standard doubles for couples up to family rooms that sleep several. Each has air-conditioning, a flat-screen TV with satellite channels, an en-suite bathroom with separate shower and toilet, a work desk and the basic essentials. What guests mention most is that most rooms look out onto the mountain or the garden — open the curtains in the morning and you get the green of Khao Ngu, which isn't easy to find at this price.
"Clean room, lovely staff, woke up to a mountain view — peaceful and quiet, and they let us bring our dog. Great value for a hillside stay."

The charm here is being a small, nature-side resort with a calm feel. There's an on-site restaurant serving Thai and local dishes for lunch and dinner, with vegetarian options, plus outdoor seating and a picnic corner to sit and catch the breeze. The detail many love most is that pets of any size are welcome, which has made it a go-to for people bringing their dogs to Ratchaburi. Free parking is on site, and there's a paid shuttle service for guests who don't drive themselves.

The location is in Ko Phlapphla, about 15-20 minutes' drive from central Ratchaburi. Beyond the stone park you can walk to, nearby sights within a short drive include the Khao Ngu hermit caves with their ancient carved Buddha images, the Khao Ngu climbing crags, Wat Mahathat Worawihan, and the Ratchaburi National Museum. If you want to push on to the Damnoen Saduak floating market or the old Khoi-Kee market, the resort works well as a base. It suits travellers who drive themselves and prefer a quiet stay close to nature over a city-centre location.

On scores, Kao Ngu Boutique Resort reviews well — but to be honest, the number of reviews is still small because it's a little resort and fairly new. Blended across platforms the real-guest average sits around 8.0 out of 10; on Agoda the handful of past guests rate it as high as about 9, but on single-digit review counts. The points praised repeatedly are friendly, attentive staff, clean rooms, lovely mountain views, a peaceful atmosphere, pet-friendliness and strong value. What to know is that this is a small, simple resort with no swimming pool, basic facilities, and it's a fair way out of town — without your own car it's hard to reach.

Honestly, Kao Ngu Boutique Resort isn't a luxury resort and never set out to be. Its appeal is being a small hillside stay with real mountain views, a quiet atmosphere, pet-friendly, for a few hundred baht. If your trip is about visiting Khao Ngu Stone Park, climbing the crags, or wanting a calm nature-side base for Ratchaburi — it lands just right. But if you want a city-centre hotel where you can walk everywhere, with a pool or the full facilities of a big resort, adjust your expectations: this is a simple little hillside resort, Ratchaburi-style.

A tip from reading plenty of reviews here: ask for a mountain-facing room when you book, because the Khao Ngu view is the highlight. If you're bringing a pet, let the resort know ahead so they can set up a suitable room. And since it's a small resort of about 14-15 rooms, long weekends or busy Khao Ngu seasons can fill up fast, so book ahead. Most importantly, plan to drive yourself — the spot is out of town and public transport barely reaches it.
